<reason>Side A won a close, high-quality debate by converting B’s free-entry floor into a comparative loss. B’s default, ratchet, and gate-versus-tools framing was the cleaner reading of the motion and forced A to defend growth of peak charges, not just parking or concerts. A still prevailed because the nurse test and the funding constraint stayed live: timed-entry and lotteries also lock out the weekend worker and raise no staff money, while pricing lots and picnics but never the sand shoves overflow onto the last free surface. B’s “budget choice” and “your concessions are the motion” lines never fully answered that usable-access comparison, so enclosure-by-ruin remained the stronger path.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s overflow reply to B’s hard line against expanding the gate: peak parking/picnic tools without pricing the sand still wreck the free lawn, exclude the nurse, and fail to hire weekend staff.</best_rebuttal>
